Agent Name: Planner
Step Number: 1
Reason for Mistake: The Planner made a critical factual error in its initial analysis by incorrectly associating the "over 60 million casualties" figure with World War I. While the Planner correctly identified that the Livesey Hall War Memorial commemorates both World War I and World War II, it erroneously concluded that World War I was the war associated with the "over 60 million" casualty count. In reality, World War II is the conflict universally recognized for having over 60 million casualties (estimates typically range from 70 to 85 million depending on the source), whereas World War I casualties are generally estimated between 15 and 20 million. This fundamental misalignment of historical data led the Planner to direct subsequent searches toward verifying World War I casualty figures, causing the entire investigation to pursue an incorrect line of reasoning.
